summary:
Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive educational storytelling platform that explores the lasting legacy of NASA's equipment left on the Moon, Mars, and throughout deep space. It transforms the stories of spacecraft, landers, rovers, scientific instruments, and exploration hardware into an engaging digital experience, revealing how these machines contributed to humanity's understanding of the Solar System and beyond.

Through an interactive Mission Archive and dedicated Mission Stories, visitors can discover the objectives, achievements, scientific contributions, and historical significance of missions such as Apollo, Surveyor, Viking, Pathfinder, Spirit, Opportunity, InSight, Dawn, Pioneer, Kepler, and Voyager.

A key feature is the Apollo Moonquake Data Explorer, designed to make historical seismic records from NASA's Apollo Passive Seismic Experiment more accessible and understandable. By connecting mission history with scientific data, the platform encourages visitors to explore not only where equipment was left behind, but also what knowledge it helped humanity gain.

The project combines interactive web technologies, visual storytelling, and educational resources to make space exploration more accessible to students and space enthusiasts. Its central message is simple: a spacecraft may stop operating, but its discoveries, scientific legacy, and contribution to exploration are never forgotten.
details:
Project Overview

Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive web-based educational experience that tells the stories of NASA equipment left on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space. Rather than treating these machines as forgotten objects, the project explores how they contributed to exploration, scientific discovery, and our understanding of the Solar System.

Main Features

  • Interactive Mission Archive: Explore historical NASA missions and equipment, including Apollo, Surveyor, Viking, Pathfinder, Spirit, Opportunity, InSight, Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker, Pioneer, Kepler, and Voyager.
  • Mission Stories: Learn about the purpose, achievements, and legacy of selected missions.
  • Apollo Moonquake Data Explorer: A data exploration feature designed around the NASA Planetary Data System's Apollo Passive Seismic Experiment event catalogue. Visitors can load the catalogue and explore its records.
  • Learning Path: Educational content designed to help students and space enthusiasts understand the science behind these missions.
  • Additional Science Exploration: Interactive educational sections covering topics such as the Solar System, planets, the Milky Way, satellites, elements, atmospheres, and habitability.

How It Works

The project is built as an interactive web experience using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Visitors can navigate between sections, explore mission records, interact with visual elements, and access linked scientific resources. The Apollo data explorer supports loading a CSV catalogue for exploration; it is intended for historical data exploration, not live spacecraft telemetry.

Intended Impact

The project aims to make space history and planetary science more accessible, especially to students. It shows how equipment that is no longer operating can still have lasting scientific and educational value.

Tools and AI Assistance

The project was developed as a web-based educational experience using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. ChatGPT was used as an AI-assisted development tool for coding support, debugging, organizing content, and improving explanations. AI assistance was reviewed and incorporated into the project by the creator. NASA mission information and scientific data are credited through the linked NASA resources. No AI-generated scientific measurements are presented as real observations.
